blocks.content: This concluding chapter consolidates names, dates and numeric facts most likely to be asked as direct one-line factual questions — ideal for last-minute revision before the exam.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu were combined into a single Union Territory on 26 January 2020.
The chapter covers important freedom fighters and political figures instrumental in the liberation of Portuguese enclaves.
Quick revision one-liners focus on key administrative, historical, and geographical milestones of DNH&DD.

cells: Last Portuguese Governor-General of the Estado da India; formally surrendered Goa, Daman and Diu to Indian forces on 19 December 1961
Long-serving (seven-time) MP from Dadra & Nagar Haveli; a dominant political figure of the territory for decades until his death in February 2021
Current (since 2024) Lok Sabha MP for Dadra & Nagar Haveli (BJP); first woman MP from the territory; wife of the late Mohanbhai Delkar
Current (since 2024) Lok Sabha MP for Daman & Diu (Independent)
Current (2026) Administrator of DNH&DD, in office since the UT's formation on 26 January 2020; also Administrator of Lakshadweep
Earlier political figure — MP from Dadra & Nagar Haveli in 1980; father of a later Congress candidate from the constituency

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Distinguish carefully between the two current MPs and their seats: Kalaben Delkar represents the ST-reserved Dadra & Nagar Haveli seat (BJP); Umesh Patel represents the unreserved Daman & Diu seat (Independent) — a commonly tested pairing.

items: DNH&DD formed 26 January 2020 by merging Dadra & Nagar Haveli (UT since 1961) and Daman & Diu (UT since 1987).
Legal instrument: The Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu (Merger of Union Territories) Act, 2019.
Capital: Daman. Largest town: Silvassa. 3 districts: Dadra & Nagar Haveli, Daman, Diu.
Total area ≈ 603 sq km; Dadra & Nagar Haveli ≈491 sq km, Daman ≈72 sq km, Diu ≈40 sq km.
Non-contiguous UT — three separate enclaves; only Dadra & Nagar Haveli borders Maharashtra (all three border Gujarat).
Diu is an island, linked to mainland Ghoghla by a bridge; Daman sits on the mainland coast.
Main river: Daman Ganga, dammed at Madhuban Dam near Silvassa.
Vegetation split: Dadra & Nagar Haveli = dry/moist deciduous forest (teak); Daman & Diu = coastal scrub, casuarina, palms, patchy mangroves.
Diu (1535) and Daman (1559) were Portuguese colonies; Dadra & Nagar Haveli came under Portuguese revenue rights via an 1779 treaty with the Maratha Peshwa.
Dadra & Nagar Haveli liberated by local uprising, 22 July 1954; self-governed 1954-61; integrated into India 11 August 1961 (Dadra and Nagar Haveli Act, 1961).
Goa, Daman & Diu annexed via Operation Vijay, 18-19 December 1961.
Goa became a full state in 1987; Daman & Diu continued as a separate UT from 30 May 1987.
No Legislative Assembly; administered by an Administrator under Article 239.
Current Administrator: Praful Khoda Patel, since 26 Jan 2020 (also Administrator of Lakshadweep).
2 Lok Sabha seats (Dadra & Nagar Haveli — ST-reserved; Daman & Diu — unreserved); 0 Rajya Sabha seats.
Judiciary under the Bombay High Court.
Dadra & Nagar Haveli = major small/medium industrial hub (engineering, plastics, pharma, chemicals).
Daman & Diu = fishing- and tourism-driven; Daman known for liberal liquor sale relative to 'dry' Gujarat.
Combined UT population ≈5.86 lakh (2011); Dadra & Nagar Haveli ≈50% Scheduled Tribe population (Dhodia, Kokna, Varli).
Varli/Warli tribe famous for Warli painting and the Tarpa dance.
Questions frequently test the merger date of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu (January 26, 2020).
Ensure clarity on key personalities who led the Vargadh, Dadra, and Silvassa liberation movements against Portuguese rule.
Diu Fort, Moti Daman Fort (St Jerome), Nani Daman Fort (St Catherine) — principal Portuguese forts.
Nagoa Beach and Devka Beach are the flagship beaches of Diu and Daman respectively.
INS Khukri Memorial, Diu — commemorates the 1971 Indo-Pak War naval loss.
Ghoghla Beach, Diu — Blue Flag certified.
Revise this chapter last — it consolidates every numeric/name fact from Chapters 1-10 in one place for rapid recall.

The two most commonly mixed-up fact pairs: (1) the 1954 local liberation of Dadra & Nagar Haveli vs the 1961 military annexation of Goa/Daman/Diu; (2) which fort belongs to Diu vs which pair belongs to Daman.
Always verify current officeholders (Administrator, both MPs) closer to your exam date, since these can change.
